entries.title: value_as_filed, value_scale and value_adjusted on every row; prev_shares_as_filed always set; mislabeled_amendment per quarter
entries.body: Tracked funds' books now keep each row's value exactly as filed (value_as_filed), the factor that turned it into whole dollars (value_scale: 1000 for a book filed in thousands, 1 for one filed in dollars, or a line-level fix such as a single line filed 1000x too large) and value_adjusted (true when value_usd differs from the filed value). Example: LSV 2026Q1 Mueller Industries (624756102) filed 161,799 and is served as $161,799,000, so value_scale is 1000. Every other filer's full book carries the same three fields: books built from the SEC 13F data sets (2026Q1 and 2026Q2) are rebuilt with them, and books read live from EDGAR are written with them from now on; a live book that was rescaled (filed in thousands or with a unit fix) and stored before this change is fetched again. Rows stored before this change keep null until their book is rebuilt; data-set books also name each row's filing (source_accession). prev_shares_as_filed is now the prior quarter's filed share count on every row with a prior, equal to prev_shares when no split applied, so it has one meaning (Amundi CRWD 2026Q3 had it null). Each quarter's book and its /v1 filing block carry mislabeled_amendment: true when a 13F-HR/A labeled NEW HOLDINGS re-filed the whole book and replaced the original (Matthew McLennan / First Eagle 2026Q2, 0001325447-26-000033; HSBC 2025Q4, 0000873630-26-000002); each amendment in filing.amendments carries the same flag.

entries.title: Every full-book row now names its filing and acceptance time; suspect_units is true or false on checked rows
entries.body: Full 13F books served by /v1 for filers outside the curated list (R2 fb/) were stored without per-row provenance, so source_accession and first_disclosed_at read null on every row (AllianceBernstein 2026Q2: all 3,467 rows). Each row now carries source_accession, the filing that first disclosed it (the original 13F-HR, or for a book with amendments the first of its filings whose information table lists the row), and first_disclosed_at, that filing's EDGAR acceptance time. An exited row names the filing that left it out. Existing books are backfilled from EDGAR acceptance times. suspect_units was set only when true and otherwise left out, so /v1 read null; every share line that goes through the cross-filer and own-prior implied-price check now reads true or false (notes, options and late-disclosed lines are not checked and stay null). AllianceBernstein 2026Q2 KLAC ($1,472 a share against a $301.71 cross-filer median) and BKNG are true. Affected: every non-curated filer's /v1 holdings and the fb/ books, from the first full run on Nov 11.

entries.title: Hedge-fund type now requires SEC Form ADV evidence
entries.body: A filer is typed hedge_fund only when (1) it is on the hand-checked list, or (2) its adviser's Form ADV (the SEC's monthly registered and exempt-reporting adviser files) shows hedge funds in Schedule D 7.B.1 whose gross assets are at least half of its regulatory AUM, or $1B and more at a quarter of it or more. SEC publishes private-fund gross assets per adviser, not per fund type, so when an adviser also runs other private funds the hedge-fund share is split by fund count and marked as an estimate. Form D filings, names and the shape of the 13F book no longer make a hedge fund on their own; such filers fall back to long_only, wealth or other. Form ADV also types wealth managers (individual clients hold most of the RAUM) and fund complexes (registered investment companies do). Name rules still type banks, brokers, market makers and ETF issuers first. Each filer's record in filer_types.json carries type_evidence with the adviser, its RAUM, hedge-fund count and gross assets. Checked against the PM's 78-row test list (all pass) and random samples of 30 hedge-fund filers (none clearly wrong).

entries.title: Holder weights use each filer's share book
entries.body: In the all-filer holder lists (stock pages' holders, data/hl/), a filer's weight in a stock was its position over its 13F total less options, which still included principal-amount notes (PRN). The methodology defines weight over the share (SH) book, as the fund pages do. Every filer's shard now carries equity_value (share positions only: no options, no notes), and holder weights divide by it. Filers with large note books moved most: Amundi's CMG weight goes from 0.000828 ($410.8M over a book including $51.4B of notes) to 0.000924, about 11% higher. Top-10 and over-5% crowding counts use the same denominator.

entries.title: Amundi's books no longer include Crédit Agricole's own 13F
entries.body: From 2024Q4 through 2026Q2, Amundi's quarterly book (CIK 1330387) also contained Crédit Agricole S.A.'s separate 13F (CIK 1191672). Amundi had filed 13F-NT notices in 2020-21 naming Crédit Agricole as its reporting manager. A rule written for Pershing Square, where one filer took over another's reporting, merged the reporter's book into every quarter Amundi also filed itself. Crédit Agricole files its own book in parallel, so its positions were counted twice. Example: 2026Q2 showed $464.9B against $415.6B on Amundi's own filings, 0001172661-26-003278 plus 0001172661-26-004047, after merging 0001172661-26-003711 (+$49.29B, 347 rows). Every 2026Q3 change measured against that quarter was wrong too: Amundi's APH prior read 17,331,344 shares instead of 15,304,334 after the 2-for-1 split, IESC 18,660 instead of 1,552, and CMG 11,331,445 instead of 10,752,786. A reporter's book is now merged in only for a real succession, when the fund's newest notice is later than its last own 13F-HR. Amundi was the only one of the 355 tracked funds affected; all-filer books never merged other filers. The publish gate now fails any book that holds another filer's 13F outside a succession, or rows from an accession that is not one of its own filings.

entries.title: Split-adjusted changes on fund pages (Egerton, Fisher)
entries.body: Some fund pages showed a 2026Q3 split as a trade because the prior quarter's shares had not been multiplied by the split ratio. Egerton's APH row read added +$492.5M; with 4,866,688 x 2 = 9,733,376 prior shares it is +975,337 shares, about +$82.2M. Fisher's APH read added (7,677 to 15,288); it is a 66-share trim. Fisher's SFBS (165,284 to 324,424) is a trim of 6,144 shares, about -$0.25M. Fisher's MNST (3,202 to 7,279) is an add of 875 shares, about +$0.04M. The causes: curated-only runs re-checked the detected splits against too few holders and dropped APH, MNST, SFBS, MLI and IESC from splits.json, and rows reused from an earlier build kept a stale split field. A split on file now drops only on a full run, and rows are rebuilt without stale fields. The publish gate fails any row that carries a split with an unadjusted prior, and any added or trimmed row whose value per share moved by about a split ratio with no split applied. IESC's 2-for-1 is confirmed by its own 8-K (0001048268-26-000131, Item 8.01, July 31 2026).

entries.title: All-filer data stalled from Nov 9 to Nov 11
entries.body: Every full refresh from Nov 9 about 20:50 UTC to Nov 11 failed the publish gate, so all-filer counts on /season/ (filers filed, the daily chart) and the holder index stayed at their Nov 9 values. Curated fund pages kept updating. The cause: the holder index treated ADRs whose 13F title reads "AMERICAN DEP" (QFIN and others) as depositary preferreds and left their holders out, so the gate correctly found fewer holders than the tracked funds alone. ADRs now count as the common stock. Separately, GitHub skipped most of the site's scheduled 10-minute rebuilds; a keepalive now rebuilds the site within 10 minutes of new data, and curated refreshes run every 10 minutes, also while a full refresh is running.

entries.title: Re-filed 13F amendments no longer double a fund's book
entries.body: Some filers re-file their whole 13F as a 13F-HR/A marked NEW HOLDINGS instead of RESTATEMENT. Copybook added those rows on top of the original, so the book was counted twice. A NEW HOLDINGS amendment that repeats more than half of the book's positions (CUSIP and put/call), or whose total is within 20% of the book's with at least half its positions, now replaces the book. Its entry in filings[] carries mislabeled_amendment: true, and the replaced filing stays in the trail with role superseded. Totals before and after, against the filing's own cover-page total: First Eagle (Matthew McLennan) 2026Q2 $120.67B to $60.75B (GOOG 14.63M to 7.32M shares; 371 positions marked added to 258); Mizuho Securities USA 2026Q2 $10.44B to $6.20B; JPMorgan Chase 2025Q3 $3,338B to $1,669B; HSBC 2025Q4 $372.1B to $196.2B; T. Rowe Price Investment Management 2025Q4 $252.8B to $158.4B; Mason Morfit 2024Q3 $8.31B to $4.37B. Also replaced: Brookfield 2024Q4 ($16.51B) and 2025Q1 ($75.38B), Check Capital 2026Q2 ($3.78B), Heard Capital 2025Q3 ($2.06B), Lingotto 2025Q3 ($5.41B), and UC Regents 2025Q2 ($1.18B), 2025Q3 ($1.84B) and 2025Q4 ($2.81B). The same rule applies to every 13F filer's book built from the SEC 13F data sets. The publish gate now fails a build when a fund's quarter exceeds 1.5 times its filed cover total, or 1.5 times its previous quarter after an amendment was added.

entries.title: Pershing Square's quarters combine both filers
entries.body: In quarters where Pershing Square Capital Management and Pershing Square Inc. (CIK 2026053) both filed a 13F-HR, Bill Ackman's book is now their sum, and the history row names the other filing in combined_with: 2026Q1 $14.28B (with 0001172661-26-002339), 2025Q4 $16.24B (with 0001172661-26-001095), 2025Q3 $15.38B (with 0001172661-25-005115). Pershing Square Inc.'s own page uses the same combined prior quarter, so its 2026Q2 HHH position (27,852,064 shares) is unchanged rather than added.

entries.title: All-filer holder counts come from every filer's full book
entries.body: The per-stock holder index across all 13F filers was built from public shards that keep each filer's 500 largest positions, so large filers such as BlackRock (5,694 positions) and Citadel (13,572) were missing from most stocks. data/hl/{issuer}.json now counts every filer's latest full 13F book, with the quarter of that book (period), the filer's type, and its change against its previous quarter where that is on file. KNSL now has 596 holders (was 236), and every stock's all-filer count is at least the number of tracked funds holding it, which the publish gate checks.

entries.title: APH and CRWD flow counts restated for the larger fund list
entries.body: The 2026-11-08 split entry gave APH as 11 bought, 9 sold and -$0.08B, but APH's 2-for-1 split was not yet in splits.json, so fund pages and alerts still showed holders as added. APH is now in splits.json, along with IESC 2-for-1 (2026Q3), and split detection requires at least 5 holders at the exact ratio, a median holder ratio of k and a price move of about 1/k. Across the tracked funds that had filed 2026Q3 by Nov 9 (82 filings), APH is 12 bought, 12 sold, -$0.25B (Solstein's exit of 825 shares is one of the sellers), and CRWD is 9 bought, 8 sold, +$0.70B.

entries.title: Tickers missing from foreign and some US holdings for about two hours
entries.body: From the 20:07 UTC data build until the 21:57 UTC build on 2026-11-08, the step that applies tickers and sectors to every fund's holdings failed, and the build published without it. Securities whose ticker comes from that step, mostly non-US-domiciled issuers with US listings plus a few US ones, showed no ticker: among others XOM (old CUSIP 30231G102), CB, LIN, STX, ASML, ETN, AZN, TT, MDT, NXPI, SPOT, FLEX, UBS, NU, KVUE and WTW. Across the 199 curated funds, holdings without a ticker rose from 2.1% to 6.0% of value (9.7% to 14.5% of rows), and 67 instead of 35 of the 602 index preview CUSIPs had none. Stock pages and Flow dropped or split those names; Exxon's CUSIP change showed as +$30.0B of buying because the exits under the old CUSIP no longer matched it (it is +$4.4B, 12 bought, 12 sold). The step was fixed at 21:57 UTC. Each build now stops before publishing if ticker coverage falls more than 0.5 percentage points, if any of the 1,000 largest CUSIPs loses its ticker, or if any required step fails; the previous data then stays live.

entries.title: Stock splits no longer count as buying
entries.body: 13F share counts are as filed, so a split made every holder look like a buyer. Copybook now detects a k-for-1 split per CUSIP when filers holding it in both quarters cluster at an exact share ratio of k, the median price moves by about 1/k, and SEC XBRL shares outstanding (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) does not contradict it. The earlier quarter's shares are then multiplied by k in every change: fund moves, Flow, stock pages, CSV change columns and alerts. Rows carry split {ratio, from_quarter, to_quarter} and prev_shares_as_filed; splits.json lists every detected split. Flow, 2026Q3 so far: CRWD (4-for-1) read 21 bought, 0 sold, +$9.13B; it is 10 bought, 6 sold, +$0.79B. APH (2-for-1) read 20 bought, 0 sold, +$5.45B; it is 11 bought, 9 sold, -$0.08B. The ICICI Prudential alert "Added: APH +$5.0M" should have read +$4.1M (70,968 shares against a split-adjusted 22,600), and its CRWD position was trimmed (16,710 against 16,840), not added. ALAB's 2026Q2 increases (Norges Bank +310%) are not a split: its price rose from about $110 to $483 and holders do not cluster at a ratio.

entries.title: Ackman's HHH was flat, not bought
entries.body: When a fund's holdings are reported by a successor or parent CIK, the prior-quarter baseline now combines every CIK that reported the fund that quarter. Bill Ackman's page showed "HHH added +$643.4M" for 2026Q2 because the baseline used only one filer's 2026Q1 book (18.85M shares); Pershing Square Inc.'s own 2026Q1 13F (0001172661-26-002339) held another 9.0M. The combined 27.85M was unchanged in 2026Q2.

entries.title: False 13D on Dan Loeb's page removed
entries.body: Third Point's Schedule 13D filings for its own private funds use placeholder CUSIPs (0000000000, 000000000). They were matched by prefix to unrelated securities, which put "New 5%+ stake: AGX Argan, 100.0% of the class" (and a 64.8% 13D/A) on Dan Loeb's page. Placeholder and all-zero CUSIPs are now dropped, the subject company is resolved by its SEC CIK first, and filings whose subject is the filer's own fund or affiliate are skipped. No placeholder match remains in any events file.

entries.title: 13D/G and Form 4 compare against the same share class
entries.body: Schedule 13D/G and Form 4 holdings were compared with the 13F position summed over every share class of the issuer. They now compare per CUSIP, and Form 4 holdings are reported per class in classes[]; classes roll up only for display. Berkshire Hathaway's Lennar Class A 13G of 2026-08-14 (13,111,741 shares) read "-298.1K vs the 13F" because the 13F's 298,117 Class B shares were added in; it is unchanged against the 13F's 13,111,741 Class A shares. The 2026-10-07 13G/A read +12.62M; it is +12.92M. Form 4s since the 13F: Class A 13.11M to 28.44M shares (about $586.4M bought at an average of about $79.4), Class B 298.1K to 568.0K (about $8.8M); the combined 29.01M figure is no longer compared with one class.

entries.title: One weight: % of the equity book
entries.body: pct_of_book is now the same number on every page, file, alert and API response: the position's value divided by the total value of the filer's share (SH) positions. Put and call options (reported at notional) and principal-amount notes (PRN, such as convertible bonds) are excluded from the denominator and shown separately with their own notional. Stock pages used to divide by the total including option notional, so Elliott's HPE stake read 6.4% on the HPE page against 10.2% on Elliott's page (LUV 5.5% against 8.7%); the one definition gives 10.2% and 8.7%. The old pct_of_book field, which held a trade's size as a share of the book, is now delta_pct_of_book. Books also carry equity_value, options_notional and prn_value. PRN rows keep their principal amount in principal_amount and count 0 shares, so notes no longer enter share-based change math.

entries.title: Positions added by a later amendment count from the amendment's acceptance time
entries.body: A 13F-HR/A NEW HOLDINGS amendment can add positions to a quarter months after the original filing, with or without a confidential-treatment request. Copybook used to merge those rows into the original filing, stamped with its date and accession, so they showed as bought in that quarter. Every holding row now carries source_accession and first_disclosed_at (the EDGAR acceptance time, UTC). Positions added by a later amendment count from the amendment's acceptance time, and quarter-over-quarter changes compare against what was public when each filing was accepted. A RESTATEMENT amendment replaces the book from its own acceptance time, and each quarter keeps the version trail of its filings. Corrected examples: Berkshire Hathaway 2025Q1 NUE ($692.7M), LEN ($221.5M) and DHI ($192.3M) were shown as new buys filed 2025-05-15 (0000950123-25-005701); they were first disclosed on 2025-08-14 20:10:02 UTC in 0000950123-25-008361. Blackstone 2025Q4 MDLN ($6.00B) was shown as filed 2026-02-17; it was disclosed on 2026-10-09 20:05:02 UTC in amendment No. 3, 0001193125-26-419075.
